name: Arakawa no Jii Sugi

location.address: Arakawa Hachimangu Shrine, 1173 Arakawa, Takahagi, Ibaraki Prefecture

access: Free. Stands within the grounds of Arakawa Hachimangu Shrine, open to the public.
transport: Roughly 15 minutes by car or taxi from JR Takahagi Station on the Joban Line.
verify_notes: Standalone destination tree, the largest and oldest known tree in Ibaraki Prefecture, designated National Natural Monument in 1924 (Taisho 13). Estimated age roughly 1,000 years, height 42m, girth approximately 10m. IMPORTANT: the tree has declined seriously in recent years, apparently from a lightning strike; the base has hollowed out and only about one-fifth of the trunk cross-section is still living tissue. Authorities (national/prefectural/municipal) removed the top 10m of the trunk to reduce load and aid preservation, and the remaining trunk is now braced with wires on three sides to prevent it toppling. It is alive today but in a fragile, actively managed state, which the story should say plainly rather than presenting it as a thriving giant. Sources: Agency for Cultural Affairs Bunkaisan Online (online.bunka.go.jp) and Ibaraki Prefectural Board of Education's own cultural-property page, both naming the same designation, age and address.
